description: Fix all backend security issues (C-1, C-2, H-1, H-2, H-3, M-4, L-1) across admin.py, auth.py, config.py, and user.py
steps: C-1: In apps/backend/app/api/v1/admin.py admin_login endpoint, change the rate-limit exception handling to raise HTTPException(status_code=503) when Redis is unavailable (same fail-closed pattern as _check_rate_limit). Currently it catches broad Exception and logs a warning then continues. Fix: re-raise 503 HTTPException if the exception is not a 429 HTTPException. Remove the fail-open comment.

C-2: In apps/backend/app/api/v1/auth.py get_current_user_optional function, after decoding the JWT and confirming token_type == 'access', add a blacklist check using Redis. Pattern: token_hash = hashlib.sha256(token.encode()).hexdigest(), then try get_redis() and check f'blacklisted_token:{token_hash}'. If blacklisted, return None. If Redis fails, pass (fail-open is acceptable for optional auth routes since they allow anonymous).

H-1: In apps/backend/app/api/v1/auth.py, update RefreshTokenRequest to add: access_token: Optional[str] = None. In refresh_token_endpoint, after generating new tokens (after new_refresh_token = create_refresh_token...), if body.access_token is provided: compute old_hash = hashlib.sha256(body.access_token.encode()).hexdigest(), decode the old access token to get its exp claim (wrap in try/except to handle invalid tokens gracefully), compute remaining_ttl = max(exp - now, 0), then if remaining_ttl > 0: await redis.set(f'blacklisted_token:{old_hash}', '1', ex=remaining_ttl, nx=True). Use the same redis import pattern as elsewhere in the file.

H-2: In apps/backend/app/api/v1/admin.py _validate_admin_session function, replace the inline algorithm logic. Currently it uses settings.JWT_ALGORITHM directly. Create a helper function _get_admin_verification_key() that returns (key, algorithm) tuple - same pattern as _get_verification_key() in auth.py. Logic: if JWT_ALGORITHM == 'RS256' and JWT_PUBLIC_KEY exists, return (JWT_PUBLIC_KEY, 'RS256'). Otherwise return (ADMIN_JWT_SECRET or JWT_SECRET, 'HS256'). Update _validate_admin_session to use this helper everywhere it decodes a JWT. Also update admin_login to use a corresponding _get_admin_signing_key() that returns the signing key and algorithm (ADMIN_JWT_SECRET or JWT_SECRET for HS256, JWT_PRIVATE_KEY for RS256).

H-3: In apps/backend/app/config.py, add a validator on TRUST_EDGE_AUTH. Use @model_validator(mode='after') pattern (since pydantic v2 with pydantic-settings). In the existing validate_production_secrets method, add a check: if self.TRUST_EDGE_AUTH and not self.EDGE_SHARED_SECRET, raise ValueError('EDGE_SHARED_SECRET must be set when TRUST_EDGE_AUTH is True'). This should apply in ALL environments, not just production.
M-4: In apps/backend/app/models/user.py, change the role field default from None to 'student': role: Optional[Literal['student', 'educator', 'staff', 'admin']] = 'student'

L-1: In apps/backend/app/api/v1/auth.py reset_password endpoint, rename the parameter from 'request' to 'body' (the function signature is: async def reset_password(request: ResetPasswordRequest)). Change to async def reset_password(body: ResetPasswordRequest). Update all references to request.token and request.new_password inside the function to body.token and body.new_password.
acceptance_criteria: admin_login rate-limit block raises 503 HTTPException when Redis is unavailable (not a 429)
get_current_user_optional checks token blacklist and returns None for blacklisted tokens
RefreshTokenRequest has optional access_token field; refresh endpoint blacklists old access token when provided
_get_admin_verification_key() and _get_admin_signing_key() helpers exist and are used in admin.py
Settings validation rejects TRUST_EDGE_AUTH=True when EDGE_SHARED_SECRET is not set
reset_password uses 'body' parameter name instead of 'request'
All Python files parse without syntax errors
findings: All 7 fixes implemented and verified via AST parsing. The H-3 fix (TRUST_EDGE_AUTH validation) will cause Settings() instantiation to fail if TRUST_EDGE_AUTH=True (the current default) and EDGE_SHARED_SECRET is not set in the environment. This is intentional security hardening - deployment must provide EDGE_SHARED_SECRET or set TRUST_EDGE_AUTH=False.
